extracted.intended_audience: health insurance issuers, plan administrators, third-party administrators, regulators, and legal counsel interpreting/applying Section 1557
extracted.subtask_description: Interpretive guidance and final-rule responses about how Section 1557 (nondiscrimination in health programs and activities) applies to health insurance coverage, benefit design, excepted benefits, and related operations of covered entities.

rubrics_metrics.name: OCR enforcement approach
rubrics_metrics.description: OCR will employ all available means of investigating health insurance coverage and other health-related coverage under this rule, including through compliance reviews and complaint investigations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR agrees that robust enforcement is critical and will not rely solely on complaints; it will engage in proactive oversight (e.g., affirmative review of plan designs) using available investigatory tools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordination with other Federal and State agencies, while retaining OCR authority
rubrics_metrics.description: OCR commits to coordinating with other Federal agencies as appropriate to avoid inconsistency and duplication in enforcement efforts and will consider issuing guidance in coordination with other agencies, such as CMS, after publication of the rule. That said, as the lead enforcement agency for section 1557, OCR maintains sole authority to determine a covered entity's compliance with this final rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR will give consideration to a covered entity's compliance with other Federal laws when those requirements overlap with section 1557's requirements and will work closely with covered entities when compliance requires additional action, but OCR's determination of compliance under Section 1557 is dispositive for Section 1557 enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with other laws is not determinative of Section 1557 compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: OCR does not view a covered entity's compliance with other State or Federal laws, which were adopted under different requirements and for different purposes, to be determinative in all cases of a covered entity's compliance with section 1557, unless otherwise specified in this rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR will consider overlapping legal requirements but will independently assess Section 1557 compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Liability of multiple entities and responsibility for subcontractors
rubrics_metrics.description: In situations where multiple covered entities provide or administer elements of a discriminatory benefit design, all of the entities may be found liable under section 1557. Both the direct recipient and subrecipient (or subcontractor) are responsible for complying with applicable civil rights laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covered entities are responsible for the conduct of their subcontractors and cannot outsource or contract away their civil rights obligations. Third-party administrators, benefits advisers, and consultants that participate in discriminatory plan design may be subject to liability where Federal financial assistance is present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissibility of programs aimed at reducing health disparities
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in this rule prohibits programs designed to improve health outcomes for specific populations so long as the programs do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, national origin, age, sex, or disability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programs may use social determinants of health or other non-protected metrics to identify underrepresented individuals; examples include Special Needs Plans. Age-distinct programs that provide special benefits to older adults or children are permitted under the Age Act and section 1557.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'health program or activity' — principal engagement covers all operations
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the definition of 'health program or activity' at §92.4, a recipient of Federal financial assistance that is principally engaged in the provision or administration of health insurance coverage or other health-related coverage is covered under this rule for all of its operations. Section 1557 applies to 'any health program or activity, any part of which is receiving Federal financial assistance.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This interpretation reasonably allows inclusion of operations such as plans offered on and off the Exchange, grandfathered and grandmothered plans, excepted benefits, STLDI, and third-party administrator activities when the issuer is principally engaged in providing or administering health coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance of Federal funds imposes nondiscrimination obligations across operations
rubrics_metrics.description: By accepting the benefit of Federal funds, a recipient is prohibited from discriminating in its health programs and activities under section 1557, including all of its operations when principally engaged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arguments about competitive disadvantage from applying Section 1557 to all operations do not abrogate statutory obligations; the prevalence of federally funded products among issuers means competitive disadvantage is unlikely to be dispositive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of specific plan types (grandfathered, grandmothered, EGWP, Medigap, self-funded non-Federal governmental plans)
rubrics_metrics.description: Grandfathered and grandmothered plans are not exempt from section 1557. Entities that receive funding through Medicare Part C or Part D (including EGWPs) are subject to the rule as recipients of Federal financial assistance. Self-funded non-Federal governmental plans are subject if they directly or indirectly receive Federal financial assistance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although grandfathered/grandmothered plans are exempt from some ACA market reforms, Section 1557 is not one of the provisions that Congress specified as excluded; OCR will consider facts and legitimate nondiscriminatory reasons in complaints. Employers or plan sponsors are excluded from liability for employment practices pursuant to §92.2(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability to excepted benefits and categories of excepted benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: Excepted benefits are statutorily defined and often exempt from ACA market reforms, but that fact does not justify their exclusion from section 1557. If a recipient health insurance issuer is principally engaged in the provision or administration of health insurance coverage or other health-related coverage, all of its operations are covered, including its provision of excepted benefits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR details types of excepted benefits (always-excepted, limited excepted benefits, independent noncoordinated excepted benefits, supplemental excepted benefits) and will evaluate alleged discriminatory design features on a case-by-case basis. A principally engaged issuer may avoid coverage for an excepted-benefits subsidiary if it proves the subsidiary is legally separate from its federally funded activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fact-specific, case-by-case investigative approach
rubrics_metrics.description: OCR's analysis for investigating a potentially discriminatory benefit design — as well as for all OCR investigations — is necessarily a fact-specific, case-by-case analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR will evaluate the nature, scope, and contours of the specific plan at issue and consider covered entities' articulated legitimate, nondiscriminatory reasons for challenged actions or practices; OCR rejects the characterization of this approach as an improper 'regulation-by-audit' without adequate notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defenses available to covered entities: legitimate nondiscriminatory reasons and fundamental alteration
rubrics_metrics.description: Covered entities have the opportunity to articulate a legitimate, nondiscriminatory basis for their challenged action or practice. In cases of alleged disability discrimination, covered entities may also prove that modifying a plan to comply with section 1557 would result in a fundamental alteration to their health program or activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of legitimate nondiscriminatory reasons include evidence that compliance with §92.207 would render a plan unaffordable or force discontinuation; OCR will carefully consider evidence to determine whether such reasons are legitimate and not pretextual.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection of market-disruption/APA notice claims without supporting evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: OCR is mindful of comments about potential market disruption and reduced health care options, but commenters did not provide sufficient evidence to support the contention that applying Section 1557 to excepted benefits would disrupt markets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR concluded the Proposed Rule provided adequate notice regarding the applicability of Section 1557 to excepted benefits (discussed in NPRM) and will not re-propose absent new supporting evidence; commenters alleging market harms must submit sufficient factual support.
